items.title: Degree-six cubic trace polynomial for a chiral representation
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
items.statement:
Let $H=SU(3)\times U(1)$, where $SU(3)=\{g\in M_3(\mathbb C):g^\dagger g=I_3,\det g=1\}$ and $U(1)=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$. For a finite-dimensional unitary representation $\rho:H\to U(V_\rho)$, let $A_\rho$ be a smooth anti-Hermitian matrix-valued one-form on a smooth manifold $X$, representing a connection in a local trivialization, and set $F_\rho=dA_\rho+A_\rho\wedge A_\rho$. Define the degree-six invariant polynomial

$$\mathcal I_6(\rho,A_\rho):=2\pi\left[\operatorname{tr}_{V_\rho}\exp\!\left(-\frac{iF_\rho}{2\pi}\right)\right]_6=\frac{i}{24\pi^2}\operatorname{tr}_{V_\rho}(F_\rho\wedge F_\rho\wedge F_\rho),$$

where the exponential is its formal power series and $[\,\cdot\,]_6$ selects the differential-form component of degree six. This is a homogeneous polynomial in the formal curvature; on a four-dimensional physical spacetime it is interpreted on the formal six-dimensional extension used for descent, not integrated as a six-form over spacetime. The normalization fixes anti-Hermitian generators, the fundamental trace, and the overall coefficient once and for all.

For the defining representation $E=\mathbb C^3$ with $\rho_E(g,z)=zg$, a background connection is $A_E=A+iB I_3$, where $A$ is an $\mathfrak{su}(3)$-valued one-form and $B$ is a real $U(1)$ connection one-form. The dual representation is $E^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(E,\mathbb C)$ with $\rho_{E^*}(g,z)=\rho_E(g,z)^{-T}$; its induced connection and curvature are $A_{E^*}=-A_E^T$ and $F_{E^*}=-F_E^T$.

references.title: Adel Bilal, Lectures on Anomalies (full lecture notes)
references.locator: §10.4, equations (10.49)–(10.54), printed pp. 87–88: anti-Hermitian connection convention and the degree-six gauge anomaly polynomial as the descent source.

references.title: Enrique Alvarez, Gauge Anomalies
references.locator: §§2.1–2.2, printed pp. 25–34: invariant-polynomial normalization, Chern–Simons transgression, and Stora–Zumino descent.

items.title: A conjugate representation reverses the cubic anomaly polynomial
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
items.statement:
Let $H=SU(3)\times U(1)$, let $E=\mathbb C^3$ have representation $\rho_E(g,z)=zg$, and let $E^*$ be its dual representation. For a smooth background connection $A_E$ on a smooth manifold $X$, use the induced dual connection $A_{E^*}=-A_E^T$ and curvatures $F_E=dA_E+A_E\wedge A_E$ and $F_{E^*}=dA_{E^*}+A_{E^*}\wedge A_{E^*}$. With the degree-six polynomial $\mathcal I_6$ defined above, one has

$$\mathcal I_6(E^*,A_{E^*})=-\mathcal I_6(E,A_E).$$

For the canonical Chern–Simons transgression

$$Q_5(E,A_E):=3\frac{i}{24\pi^2}\int_0^1\operatorname{tr}_E\!\left(A_E\wedge F_{E,t}\wedge F_{E,t}\right)\,dt,\qquad F_{E,t}:=t\,dA_E+t^2A_E\wedge A_E,$$

the dual transgression satisfies $Q_5(E^*,A_{E^*})=-Q_5(E,A_E)$. Thus any common linear descent of this conjugate pair has zero total cubic polynomial and zero total first consistent descent representative.

references.title: Adel Bilal, Lectures on Anomalies (full lecture notes)
references.locator: §§7.1–7.2 and 9.4, printed pp. 45–50 and 75–77: complex-conjugate representations and the representation trace in the four-dimensional anomaly polynomial.

references.title: Enrique Alvarez, Gauge Anomalies
references.locator: §§2.2–2.3, printed pp. 30–36: linear descent from an invariant polynomial, additivity, and the sign reversal for conjugate representation indices.

items.title: A local counterterm changes only the representative of a local anomaly class
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
items.statement: Let $\mathcal A_U^{g,p}$ be the finite-jet horizontal-form spaces on a smooth open set $U\subseteq\mathbb R^4$, with nilpotent BRST differential $s$, horizontal differential $d_H$, and $sd_H+d_Hs=0$. In bidegree $(1,4)$, define $H^{1,4}(s\mid d_H)$ as the ghost-number-one four-forms $a_4$ satisfying $sa_4+d_Hb_3=0$ for some $b_3$, modulo the subspace $\{sC_4+d_Hr_3:C_4\in\mathcal A_U^{0,4},\ r_3\in\mathcal A_U^{1,3}\}$. If a local counterterm changes an anomaly representative from $a_4$ to $a'_4=a_4+sC_4+d_Hr_3$, then $[a'_4]=[a_4]$ in $H^{1,4}(s\mid d_H)$.

references.title: Adel Bilal, Lectures on Anomalies (full lecture notes)
references.locator: §§9.2 and 9.4, printed pp. 71–77: local BRST coboundaries, consistent anomaly representatives, and the local-counterterm ambiguity.

references.title: Enrique Alvarez, Gauge Anomalies
references.locator: §2.4, printed pp. 36–38: a local Bardeen–Zumino counterterm changes the consistent/covariant representative while preserving the underlying local anomaly data.

items.title: Local perturbative ’t Hooft anomaly modulo counterterms
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
items.statement:
Fix a four-dimensional smooth spacetime region $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with a stated orientation, spin structure, boundary conditions, and unit system. A selected model specifies a continuous global symmetry group $H$, its action on the fields and observables, the nondynamical background connections, the field and jet domains, a regulator and measure or formal perturbative generating functional, and the admissible local counterterms. A background connection is nondynamical model data: it transforms under local changes of background trivialization but is not integrated over.

Let $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{g,p}$ be the finite-jet horizontal $p$-forms of ghost number $g$ generated by the nondynamical background connections and their BRST ghost jets, without matter-field jets, and restrict the model’s nilpotent BRST differential $s$ and horizontal exterior derivative $d_H$ to this background subalgebra. An infinitesimal local anomaly representative is a local horizontal four-form $a_4\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{1,4}$ such that $sa_4+d_Hb_3=0$ for some $b_3\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{2,3}$. The **local perturbative ’t Hooft anomaly** of the specified global symmetry is the class $[a_4]$ in the relative cohomology $H^{1,4}(s\mid d_H)$ of this background subalgebra, with the quotient taken using exactly the model’s admissible four-dimensional background counterterms and total-derivative boundary convention. Its class is zero exactly when an admissible local counterterm removes the infinitesimal background variation modulo a boundary term.

This definition applies to a global symmetry whose background is nondynamical. If the same local class concerns a field integrated over as a gauge redundancy, it is a local gauge anomaly, not a ’t Hooft anomaly; an uncancelled gauge anomaly obstructs the proposed gauging unless a separately specified cancellation mechanism is included. The definition addresses only infinitesimal transformations and makes no claim about large or disconnected transformations, determinant-line holonomy, torsion phases, or a physical continuum limit.

references.title: Adel Bilal, Lectures on Anomalies (full lecture notes)
references.locator: §§4.1, 9.1–9.4, and 10.4, printed pp. 18–27 and 69–88: effective-action variation, consistent BRST descent, counterterm ambiguity, and the local/global scope boundary.

references.title: Enrique Alvarez, Gauge Anomalies
references.locator: §§2.1–2.4, printed pp. 25–38: the local BRST descent, representation-dependent polynomial, and counterterm changes between consistent and covariant representatives.

items.physical_scope: A definition of the infinitesimal, local anomaly class of a specified background-coupled global symmetry in four dimensions; it asserts no global-anomaly classification, continuum QFT existence, or automatic gauging.

items.title: Flat-space chiral anomaly-matching data and regulator convention
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
items.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ and flat oriented Minkowski spacetime $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-,+,+,+)$ and its standard spin structure. Fix Dirac matrices by $\{\gamma^\mu,\gamma^\nu\}=2\eta^{\mu\nu}I$ and $\gamma_5=i\gamma^0\gamma^1\gamma^2\gamma^3$; set $P_+=(I+\gamma_5)/2$ and $P_-=I-P_+$. The global symmetry group is the fixed global form $H=SU(3)\times U(1)_V$, acting on a finite multiset $S$ of massless positive-chirality Weyl fields. Each field is a Grassmann-odd smooth compactly supported section of $\operatorname{im}(P_+)\otimes V_i$, where $V_i$ carries a specified finite-dimensional unitary representation $R_i$ of $H$. The chiral kinetic operator is $\mathcal D_{+,i}=P_-i\gamma^\mu D_{\mu,i}P_+$ from positive to negative chirality; its regulated determinant phase is a formal perturbative input. The matter field has mass dimension $3/2$; the background potentials have mass dimension one, their curvature two-forms dimension two, and all $U(1)_V$ charges and trace coefficients are dimensionless. The backgrounds are global one-forms on the trivial bundles over $M$, vary smoothly, and have compact support; the global symmetry is not integrated over as a dynamical gauge redundancy.

For each species, the background covariant derivative is $D_{\mu,i}=\partial_\mu+\rho_{i*}(A_\mu,iB_\mu)$ in its representation, where $A$ is an anti-Hermitian $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ connection, $B$ is a real $U(1)_V$ connection, and $\rho_{i*}:\mathfrak{su}(3)\oplus i\mathbb R\to\mathfrak u(V_i)$ is the derived Lie-algebra representation. Set $F_A=dA+A\wedge A$ and $f=dB$, and write $A_i:=\rho_{i*}(A,iB)$ and $F_i:=dA_i+A_i\wedge A_i$; thus $D_{\mu,i}=\partial_\mu+(A_i)_\mu$. For $E=(\mathbf3,+1)$, $A_E=A+iB I_3$ and $F_E=F_A+ifI_3$; for $E^*=(\bar{\mathbf3},-1)$, $A_{E^*}=-A^T-iB I_3$ and $F_{E^*}=-F_A^T-ifI_3$. Local transformations are $A\mapsto g^{-1}Ag+g^{-1}dg$ and $B\mapsto B+d\alpha$ for compactly supported $g: M\to SU(3)$ and $\alpha:M\to\mathbb R$; the $U(1)$ group element is $e^{i\alpha}$. Let $c$ be the ghost-number-one odd $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ ghost and $\eta$ the ghost-number-one odd real $U(1)_V$ ghost. The finite-jet BRST differential for $\mathfrak h=\mathfrak{su}(3)\oplus i\mathbb R$ is $sA=dc+[A,c]$, $sc=-[c,c]/2$, $sB=d\eta$, $s\eta=0$, and $s\psi_i=-\rho_{i*}(c,i\eta)\psi_i$; it acts on jets by commuting with total derivatives. The $U(1)_V$ factor is central, so these are the direct-sum Lie-algebra BRST formulas.

The anomaly-matching data include one common Pauli–Villars subtraction prescription for the chiral triangle graphs, with opposite-statistics regulator fields and regulator masses taken to the large-mass limit, together with the consistent effective-action variation convention and compact-support boundary conditions. The local anomaly complex is the finite-jet background subalgebra generated by $A,B$ and their BRST ghosts, with no matter-field jets, so its ghost-number-zero four-forms are precisely the admitted local counterterms. We quotient by all such finite-jet local counterterms and by compactly supported total derivatives; no background-gauge-invariance condition is imposed on an individual counterterm. In particular, for real dimensionless $\lambda$, the four-form $C_4=\lambda B\wedge K_3(A)$ is admitted, where $K_3(A):=\operatorname{tr}(A\wedge dA+\tfrac23A\wedge A\wedge A)$. As an explicit source-backed one-loop input, after the regulator masses are taken to infinity this selected prescription assigns to each positive-chirality species $R_i$ the consistent local anomaly obtained by descent from $\mathcal I_6(R_i,A_i)$ of the preceding cubic-polynomial definition. The fixed linear descent map is normalized by $\mathcal I_6=dI^{(0)}_5$, $sI^{(0)}_5+d_HI^{(1)}_4=0$, and $sI^{(1)}_4+d_HI^{(2)}_3=0$, with $\delta\Gamma=\sum_{i\in S}\int_M I^{(1)}_4(R_i,A_i)$. This determinant law is an adopted regulator input in the data, not a locally derived theorem about every regulator. The total polynomial is $\mathcal I_6^{\mathrm{tot}}=\sum_{i\in S}\mathcal I_6(R_i,A_i)$, and its local anomaly class is interpreted using the preceding local ’t Hooft-anomaly definition. No large-transformation test, torsion calculation, mixed gravitational term, dynamical gauge quantization, or continuum-existence result is included.

items.title: Local anomaly cancellation for a conjugate chiral pair
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
items.statement:
Use the selected flat-space anomaly-matching model on oriented $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-,+,+,+)$ and natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Its nondynamical global-symmetry backgrounds are a smooth compactly supported anti-Hermitian $SU(3)$ connection $A$ and a smooth compactly supported real $U(1)_V$ connection $B$ on the trivial bundles. The finite field spectrum consists of two massless positive-chirality Weyl species, one in $E=(\mathbf3,+1)$ and one in its dual $E^*=(\bar{\mathbf3},-1)$. The background is not integrated over. Use one common large-mass Pauli–Villars subtraction scheme and the consistent effective-action convention fixed in the model data.

Adopt the source-backed one-loop input that each positive-chirality species in this regulator has consistent local variation given by descent from $\mathcal I_6(R)=2\pi[\operatorname{tr}_R\exp(-iF_R/(2\pi))]_6$, with the same linear descent for every species: $\mathcal I_6=dI_5^{(0)}$, $sI_5^{(0)}+d_HI_4^{(1)}=0$, and $sI_4^{(1)}+d_HI_3^{(2)}=0$, and $\delta\Gamma=\sum_R\int_M I_4^{(1)}(R)$. Here $s$ is the infinitesimal background BRST differential. The local anomaly class is the class of $I_4^{(1)}$ in $H^{1,4}(s\mid d_H)$: local ghost-number-one four-forms satisfying the second descent equation, modulo $s$-variations of admitted local counterterms and total derivatives.

Then the total perturbative local anomaly class of this conjugate pair vanishes. This conclusion concerns only the identity component of the background-transformation group in the adopted one-loop convention; it asserts no absence of large-transformation or torsion anomalies and no consistency result for a dynamical gauge redundancy.

items.physical_scope: A conditional one-loop result for infinitesimal background transformations of the stated flat-space SU(3)×U(1) global symmetry in one common large-mass Pauli–Villars subtraction convention. It proves only vanishing of the perturbative local class for the conjugate pair; it does not test global anomalies, establish a dynamical gauge theory, or construct a continuum QFT.

title: Perturbative ’t Hooft Anomalies and Counterterms — Examples

items.title: A single chiral fundamental has a nonzero local polynomial
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
items.statement:
Use the same flat-space background convention but take the spectrum to contain only one positive-chirality species $E=(\mathbf3,+1)$. Its polynomial is

$$\mathcal I_6(E)=\frac{i}{24\pi^2}\left(\operatorname{tr}F_A^3+3i f\wedge\operatorname{tr}F_A^2+3(if)^3\right),$$

where $F_A$ is the anti-Hermitian $SU(3)$ curvature, $f=dB$ is the $U(1)_V$ curvature, and the expression is evaluated as a degree-six polynomial on the formal extension used for descent. The mixed $U(1)_V$–$SU(3)^2$ term and the pure $U(1)_V^3$ term have nonzero coefficients. This example verifies that the one-field polynomial is not the zero invariant polynomial; it does not claim that the associated relative BRST class is nontrivial modulo every admissible counterterm or that a global anomaly has been evaluated.

items.title: A mixed-background counterterm shifts the local representative
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
items.statement:
Let $A$ be a smooth compactly supported anti-Hermitian $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ connection one-form on trivial $\mathbb R^{1,3}$, with curvature $F_A=dA+A\wedge A$, and let $B$ be a smooth real $U(1)_V$ background one-form with compactly supported gauge parameter $\alpha$. In natural units, $[A]=[B]=\text{mass}$ and $[F_A]=\text{mass}^2$. Define the local three-form

$$K_3(A):=\operatorname{tr}\left(A\wedge dA+\frac23A\wedge A\wedge A\right)$$

and add the four-dimensional local counterterm $C_4=\lambda B\wedge K_3(A)$ to the effective action, with dimensionless coefficient $\lambda$. Under the $U(1)_V$ background transformation $B\mapsto B+d\alpha$ with $A$ fixed, its local variation is

$$\delta_\alpha C_4=\lambda\,d(\alpha K_3(A))-\lambda\,\alpha\operatorname{tr}(F_A\wedge F_A).$$

The first term integrates to a boundary term and vanishes for compactly supported $\alpha$. Thus this counterterm shifts the $U(1)_V$ component of the local anomaly representative by $-\lambda\alpha\operatorname{tr}(F_A\wedge F_A)$ while the full relative class is unchanged modulo the admitted counterterm space. This calculation does not assert that the full $SU(3)\times U(1)_V$ anomaly vanishes or that the $SU(3)$ component of the representative is unchanged.

items.title: A conjugate SU(3)×U(1) chiral pair with zero local polynomial
items.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
items.statement:
Use the flat four-dimensional background data with global group $SU(3)\times U(1)_V$ and the common consistent regulator fixed above. Take the finite spectrum to consist of positive-chirality Weyl species $E=(\mathbf3,+1)$ and $E^*=(\bar{\mathbf3},-1)$. On a formal six-dimensional extension, write the anti-Hermitian $SU(3)$ curvature as $F_A$ and the $U(1)_V$ curvature as $f=dB$. The defining-representation curvature is $F_E=F_A+i f I_3$, with $\operatorname{tr}F_A=0$, so

$$\mathcal I_6(E)=\frac{i}{24\pi^2}\left(\operatorname{tr}F_A^3+3i f\wedge\operatorname{tr}F_A^2+3(if)^3\right).$$

The dual species has the opposite polynomial. The total polynomial and its common linear consistent descent therefore vanish, so this example has zero perturbative local anomaly class in the selected scheme. The six-dimensional extension is only the formal degree-six polynomial domain; the physical model remains four-dimensional.
